docs.title: Case Converter
docs.text:
Case Converter converts a string into one of 13 naming formats. Create a Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert instance with the source string, optionally you can also use the factory class.

The Convert class was designed to be immutable, the source cannot be changed after construction.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the package with Composer.

composer require jawira/case-converter

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
The library detects the input format automatically:

use Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert;

$convert = new Convert('The-Terminator');

echo $convert->toPascal(); // TheTerminator
echo $convert->toCobol();  // THE-TERMINATOR
echo $convert->toSnake();  // the_terminator

See all supported formats and methods.

docs.title: Choose the input format
docs.text:
Automatic detection follows a fixed order. If the format is known, use the matching from*() method to control how the original string is split:

$convert = new Convert('FBI');

$convert->fromAda()->toSnake();   // fbi: one word separated by underscores
$convert->fromCamel()->toSnake(); // f_b_i: split before each uppercase letter

from*() methods return the same object and can be chained with conversion methods. See automatic format detection for the rules.

docs.title: Inspect the input
docs.text:
getSource() returns the original string, and toArray() returns the words currently detected from it:

$convert = new Convert('Mario Bros');

$convert->getSource(); // Mario Bros
$convert->toArray();   // ['Mario', 'Bros']

docs.title: Unicode case mapping
docs.text:
The library supports Unicode case conversion. By default it uses full case mapping, which can change a string's length. Call forceSimpleCaseMapping() to request simple case mapping instead:

$convert = new Convert('Straße');

$convert->toUpper(); // STRASSE
$convert->forceSimpleCaseMapping()->toUpper(); // STRAßE

See case mapping for details and limitations.

docs.title: Use the factory
docs.text:
This library also provides \Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverter as a factory. Call convert() to create a Convert instance:

use \Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverter;

$cc = new CaseConverter();

// Convert string to Pascal case
$cc->convert('XML')->toPascal(); // Xml

// Convert string to Snake case
$cc->convert('v3.0.2')->toSnake(); // v3_0_2

// Convert string to Camel case
$cc->convert('first-name')->toCamel(); // firstName

// Convert from Lower case to Dot case
$cc->convert('non-SI units')->fromLower()->toDot(); // non-si.units

// Get detected words
$cc->convert('Mario Bros')->toArray(); // ['Mario', 'Bros']

// Retrieve original string
$cc->convert('use_the_force')->getSource(); // use_the_force

For dependency injection, CaseConverter implements CaseConverterInterface.

use Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverterInterface;

final class NameFormatter
{
    public function __construct(private CaseConverterInterface $cc) {}

    public function format(string $slug): string
    {
        return $this->cc->convert($slug)->toCamel();
    }
}

See using the factory for framework configuration.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Convert stores the source string and the words extracted from it. Construct it with the string to convert; the format is detected automatically unless you select a splitter with a from*() method. Conversion methods return strings.

use Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert;

$convert = new Convert('first-name');
$convert->toCamel(); // firstName

Convert is immutable with respect to its source string: getSource() always returns the original input. from*() methods update the detected words on the same instance and return that instance, so calls can be chained.

docs.title: Input format methods
docs.text:
These methods tell the converter how to split the original source string. They return the same Convert instance. Delimited formats split on one or more of the named delimiter characters; camel and Pascal formats split before each uppercase letter.

Method(s) Splitting rule fromAuto() Detect the format using the detection algorithm fromCamel(), fromPascal() Before uppercase letters fromSnake(), fromAda(), fromMacro() Underscores (_) fromKebab(), fromTrain(), fromCobol() Hyphens (-) fromLower(), fromUpper(), fromTitle(), fromSentence() Spaces fromDot() Dots (.)

The names in each row use the same splitting rule; the source's capitalization does not affect how words are split.

fromAuto() accepts an optional $digitsAreLowercase argument, which defaults to true. With the default, digits are grouped with lowercase text when detecting uppercase-only input. Set it to false to treat digits like uppercase letters for this check.

docs.title: Utility methods
docs.text: Method Description getSource() Return the original input string. toArray() Return the currently detected words as an array of strings. forceSimpleCaseMapping() Use simple rather than full Unicode case mapping for subsequent conversions; returns this instance.

docs.title: Unicode case mapping
docs.text:
Case mapping changes letters between uppercase, lowercase, and title case. The Unicode standard defines simple and full mappings:

  • Simple mapping maps one code point to one code point.
  • Full mapping may map one code point to multiple code points.

For example, full uppercase mapping converts the German ß to SS, while simple mapping leaves it as ß. Case Converter uses full mapping by default.

use Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert;

$value = new Convert('Straße');

$value->toUpper(); // STRASSE
$value->forceSimpleCaseMapping()->toUpper(); // STRAßE

forceSimpleCaseMapping() returns the same object. It affects subsequent conversion calls on that object; it does not change the detected words or the source string.

docs.title: Locale-specific behavior
docs.text: Case Converter uses PHP's mb_convert_case() with UTF-8. The library does not accept a locale setting, so locale-specific casing rules, such as Turkish dotted and dotless i, are not selected based on the user's locale.

docs.title: Evolution of Case-Mapping in PHP
docs.text:
PHP 7.3 introduced full case-mapping, you can have one-to-many character mapping. In practice this means than you can have different results depending on your PHP version.

Internally Case-Converter uses mb_convert_case () . This function works in conjunction with specific constants to tell what action to perform. For example:

mb_convert_case('Foo', MB_CASE_UPPER); // FOO

Prior to PHP 7.3, these were the available constants and their use:

Constant Meaning MB_CASE_UPPER Performs simple upper-case fold conversion. MB_CASE_LOWER Performs simple lower-case fold conversion. MB_CASE_TITLE Performs simple title-case fold conversion.

But from PHP 7.3, new constants were added and their meaning changed:

Constant Meaning MB_CASE_UPPER Performs a full upper-case folding. MB_CASE_LOWER Performs a full lower-case folding. MB_CASE_TITLE Performs a full title-case conversion. MB_CASE_UPPER_SIMPLE Performs simple upper-case fold conversion. MB_CASE_LOWER_SIMPLE Performs simple lower-case fold conversion. MB_CASE_TITLE_SIMPLE Performs simple title-case fold conversion.

docs.title: Automatic format detection
docs.text:
When a Convert object is created, the library splits the source string into words. fromAuto() reruns this detection on the original source. Detection chooses the first matching rule below:

  1. If the string contains an underscore (_), split on one or more underscores.
  2. Otherwise, if it contains a hyphen (-), split on one or more hyphens.
  3. Otherwise, if it contains a space (␣), split on one or more spaces.
  4. Otherwise, if it contains a dot (.), split on one or more dots.
  5. Otherwise, if the whole string contains only uppercase letters, treat it as one word.
  6. Otherwise, split before every uppercase letter.

The diagram below illustrates the detection order.

The order matters. For example, if a string contains both underscores and hyphens, automatic detection uses underscores and leaves hyphens inside the resulting words. Choose an explicit from*() method when the source format is known or when the automatic result is not what you want.

Tip

By default, digits count like lowercase characters in the uppercase-only check. For example, fromAuto() treats ABC123 as one word. Pass false to fromAuto(false) to count digits like uppercase characters in that check. This option affects only automatic detection of uppercase-only strings.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation site is built with MkDocs. To build it locally, install MkDocs with the Material theme, then run phing docs:build. To preview changes while editing, run phing docs:serve.

docs:build also refreshes generated diagrams, so the project's development dependencies must be installed first.

docs.title: Using Phing behind a proxy
docs.text: If you are developing behind a proxy, configure the http_proxy environment variable. build.xml passes it to Phing tasks that need it.

docs.title: Creating new convention
docs.text:
1. Create new Gluer class.
  2. Create new Split class.
  3. Update \Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert::analyse if needed.
  4. Register into \Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert::handleSplitterMethod.
  5. Register into \Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert::handleGluerMethod.
  6. Update docblock \Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert to register new methods.
  7. Update documentation.

docs.title: Digits and word boundaries
docs.text:
Digits are not treated as word separators. In automatic detection, digits are also treated like lowercase characters by default when checking whether an input consists only of uppercase letters. This can make strings containing digits split differently than expected:

use Jawira\CaseConverter\Convert;

(new Convert('REEL2REAL'))->toDot(); // r.e.e.l2.r.e.a.l
(new Convert('reel2real'))->toDot(); // reel2real
(new Convert('Reel2Real'))->toDot(); // reel2.real

For example, hello8World converts to hello8-world in kebab case. The converter cannot infer that the 8 should have been a separate word. If a particular split is required, preprocess the input to add a separator where needed.

docs.title: Acronyms and mixed capitalization
docs.text:
The converter splits before every uppercase letter in unseparated input. It does not infer acronym boundaries.

For example, XMLHttpRequest is split as X, M, L, Http, Request, and converts to x.m.l.http.request in dot notation. If the intended words are Xml, Http, and Request, write the input as XmlHttpRequest.

❌ Wrong ✅ Good PHP_CodeSniffer php_code_sniffer PHP_CodeSniffer PhpCodeSniffer PHPUnit PhpUnit PHPUnit php-unit

Use consistent separators and capitalization in the source. For example, PHP_CodeSniffer mixes an acronym with an underscore-separated name, while php_code_sniffer and PhpCodeSniffer have unambiguous boundaries.

Acronyms in PHP

This acronym problem has also affected PHP's own class naming conventions. A 2024 PHP RFC on acronym casing was accepted to treat acronyms and initialisms like regular words in Pascal case: for example, prefer HttpRequest over HTTPRequest. The RFC updates PHP's policy for internal classes; it does not rename existing classes. This mixed-case style also makes word boundaries easier for Case Converter to detect.

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text:
Naming conventions are also called naming styles or case conventions. This page describes the formats produced by Case Converter. Word boundaries are shown with the relevant separator; camel and Pascal case join words without a separator.

Format Example Word separator Camel case myNameIsBond None; first word starts lowercase Pascal case MyNameIsBond None; each word starts uppercase Snake case my_name_is_bond Underscore; lowercase Ada case My_Name_Is_Bond Underscore; title case Macro case MY_NAME_IS_BOND Underscore; uppercase Kebab case my-name-is-bond Hyphen; lowercase Train case My-Name-Is-Bond Hyphen; title case Cobol case MY-NAME-IS-BOND Hyphen; uppercase Dot notation my.name.is.bond Dot; lowercase Lower case my name is bond Space; lowercase Title case My Name Is Bond Space; title case Upper case MY NAME IS BOND Space; uppercase Sentence case My name is bond Space; first word title case, remaining words lowercase

Capitalization follows Unicode case-mapping rules. See Case mapping.

docs.title: Using the factory
docs.text:
The package provides Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverter and the CaseConverterInterface. The factory's convert() method creates a new Convert instance for the supplied source string.

Using the interface in your services makes the dependency easy to configure and replace in tests:

namespace App;

use Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverterInterface;

final class NameFormatter
{
    public function __construct(private CaseConverterInterface $converter) {}

    public function variableName(string $text): string
    {
        return $this->converter->convert($text)->toCamel();
    }

    public function constantName(string $text): string
    {
        return $this->converter->convert($text)->fromKebab()->toMacro();
    }
}

In Symfony, register CaseConverterInterface as a service and use autowiring to inject it through the interface.

The factory can also be instantiated directly:

use Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverter;

$converter = new CaseConverter();
$result = $converter->convert('first-name')->toCamel(); // firstName

Using the factory \Jawira\CaseConverter\CaseConverter::convert is preferred because:

  • Usually the new operator is considered harmful.
  • You can easily mock dependencies when writing tests.
  • It's SOLID.
